theme: 健康-节日工作者的职业耗竭

content.text: Shi An, you previously suggested I try meditation for wellness, and I've actually started practicing it recently! Look, here's a group photo from our community yoga class—twice a week, and it feels incredibly relaxing.

Great, Happy New Year! It's wonderful to see you actively participating in group activities, which aligns perfectly with your value of connecting with the community. Yoga really does help balance the mind and body. Have you noticed any improvement in your sleep lately?
Yes! I used the sleep app you recommended to track my sleep, and the data has improved significantly. Look, my deep sleep time has increased, and the number of times I wake up has decreased.

I'm glad to see your sleep quality has improved; it has indeed been very helpful. Regular exercise combined with meditation is effective in alleviating professional burnout. Do you feel any other changes?
Well, I feel more energetic and less irritable than when I was planning events before. However, I still sometimes worry that exercising takes up too much time and affects my work progress.

This is perfectly normal, He Sui. Remember our discussion about rhythm and balance? Exercise isn't a burden; it's about infusing energy into your work. You can think of it as a form of 'self-ritual,' much like the light ritual New Year's Eve dinner you planned.
You're right! I've recently taken up cycling, heading out to the suburbs on weekends, and it feels incredibly freeing. Look, here's a photo from last week of me cycling on a mountain trail.

Outdoor activities are fantastic—they allow you to connect with nature and relieve urban stress. This reminds me of the Yuanbao incident, where you mentioned that pets also need time to adapt to their environment. In fact, it’s the same for people; we need diverse activities to stay energized.

Haha, indeed! But cycling can be quite tiring sometimes. At first, I always wanted to set strict plans, but later I found that being more spontaneous actually makes it more enjoyable. Does this count as breaking my 'festival frenzy' mode?

This is a healthy adjustment, a New Year's blessing. Enthusiasm can drive innovation, but excess can lead to exhaustion. You are now able to balance ritual and self-care, which is precisely the 'toolbox' mindset we emphasized when collaborating on the guide.
I also tried skiing! Although I'm just a beginner, the feeling of gliding down the snowy slope was amazing. Look, here's a photo my friend took of me.
I'm really happy for you, happy New Year! Trying new sports can spark curiosity and avoid monotony. However, be careful when skiing and don't get too carried away like you do when planning events.

Don't worry, I've learned to act within my capabilities now. After these exercises, I feel much more relaxed physically, have more energy every day, and even feel more creative when planning community activities.

This is precisely the virtuous cycle of self-care. Exercise improves physical health, enhances emotional well-being, and in turn boosts work efficiency. The journey from burnout to recovery is highly instructive.
Yes, I now feel that 'self-rituals' are just as important as traditional rituals. I used to be so busy creating meaning for others that I neglected myself. Thank you for your support, Shian!
You're welcome, and happy New Year. I'm glad to see your situation improving. This makes me think that perhaps we could include 'self-rituals' in future guide updates to help more holiday workers.
Great idea! I can share experiences from the sports community, and you can provide psychological adjustment advice. Just like the previous collaboration guide, we'll combine tradition and innovation.
Yes, maintain this collaborative rhythm. Remember, balance is key—whether in exercise or work, don't let plans become a burden. You're doing great right now, keep it up!

I will! I feel like I've regained my rhythm, and both my body and mind feel lighter. This must be what you mean by 'authentic connection'—first connecting well with myself, so I can better connect with the community.
Well said, Hesui. I'm glad to see that you've not only improved your physical health but also gained new insights in your mindset. Keep it up, and let's catch up next time!
